project_option: Project 1 - ImmXrsive Talent and Industry Platform
notes: Routes are grouped: /api/* is public, /api/my/* requires a signed-in verified student and resolves ownership server-side from the session. Describing a check here does not claim it passes; it tells a reviewer where to reproduce it.

checks.method_or_action: Sign in, then use the single Add Project form and choose Save project
checks.setup: A student profile must exist; create one at /profile-edit.html first
checks.expected_behavior: One project is created as a private draft and the browser lands on /project-edit.html?id=<new id>. The draft is not publicly readable: GET /api/projects/<id> returns 404 until it is published.

checks.method_or_action: POST with title, description, domain, date_text, technologies, repositories, role; demo links are set afterwards via PUT
checks.setup: Session cookie sid for a verified student who has a profile
checks.expected_behavior: Title, description, domain/type, technologies, date/status, public links and media/demo fields are all stored and returned by GET /api/my/projects/{id}.

checks.method_or_action: POST {"repository": "https://github.com/Rudra2211/team08-immxrsive"}
checks.setup: None beyond a verified session; the repository must be public
checks.expected_behavior: Returns {suggestions: {title, description, repository, technologies, links}} drawn from the repository's public metadata and languages. Nothing is created or saved. Every value is editable in the form before Save project.

checks.method_or_action: Add two repositories, then delete both
checks.setup: A project created by this student
checks.expected_behavior: A project holds zero, one or many repositories. After removing every repository the project is still valid and GET /api/projects/{id} still returns it with its title, contributors and demo links.

checks.method_or_action: Open the one project id from each contributor's profile
checks.setup: A published project with two accepted contributors
checks.expected_behavior: Both contributors' profiles link to the SAME project id and the same public URL. No per-contributor duplicate project record exists.

checks.method_or_action: Attempt a shared-field update as an accepted contributor who is not the maintainer
checks.setup: A project maintained by a different student
checks.expected_behavior: 403. Team decision: the maintainer is the only authorized editor of shared fields. The project editor shows those fields read-only and says a teammate maintains the project. The contributor's own statement remains editable.

checks.method_or_action: POST {"student_id": "<accepted contributor id>"}
checks.setup: A project with at least one accepted contributor besides the maintainer
checks.expected_behavior: Maintenance moves to that contributor. The project id and public URL are unchanged, no new record is created, every contributor relationship survives, and the former maintainer then receives 403 on shared-field updates. Transfer to a non-contributor returns 400.

checks.method_or_action: POST {"student_id", "role"}; teammates are found via GET /api/students/search?q=
checks.setup: The invited student must already have an account on the platform
checks.expected_behavior: A contributor row is created with status 'invited' and the proposed standardized role. A role outside data/standard_roles.json is refused with 400.

checks.method_or_action: POST {"accept": true} or {"accept": false} as the invited student
checks.setup: A pending invitation, visible at /my-projects.html
checks.expected_behavior: Before the answer, GET /api/projects/{id} does NOT list the invited student among contributors. After accept they appear with their role; after decline they never appear. A student who is not the invitee receives 403 on this route.

checks.method_or_action: GET the vocabulary; PUT {"role"} as maintainer
checks.setup: An accepted contributor
checks.expected_behavior: options.roles is exactly the 12 roles from standard_roles.json. An accepted contributor carries one standardized role plus an optional personal contribution statement.

checks.method_or_action: PUT {"contribution_statement", "featured"} as the contributor; then attempt to change it as the maintainer
checks.setup: Two students, one maintainer and one accepted contributor
checks.expected_behavior: The statement is written only by its owner. No route accepts another student's contribution_statement: the maintainer's role route ignores the field, so the contributor's text is unchanged after the maintainer saves.

checks.method_or_action: Untick 'Show this project on my profile' and save
checks.setup: A published project the contributor has accepted
checks.expected_behavior: The project disappears from that student's public profile projects list, while GET /api/projects/{id} still credits them as a contributor. The accepted relationship is untouched and can be re-featured.

checks.method_or_action: Remove a contributor as maintainer, then restore them
checks.setup: An accepted contributor with a contribution statement
checks.expected_behavior: Team decision: removal is a reversible soft delete. The row persists with removed_at set, the contribution statement is preserved, the contributor is hidden from public pages, and restore returns them with their statement intact. A single unilateral action therefore cannot destroy the relationship. Removing the maintainer is refused with 409 until maintenance is transferred.

checks.method_or_action: Compare the project's technologies with each contributor's skills
checks.setup: A project whose technologies include values absent from the contributors' skill lists
checks.expected_behavior: Project technologies never appear in any contributor's personal skills. student_skills and project_technologies are separate tables and no route writes the latter into the former. The project page states this in words.

checks.method_or_action: Open the public project page as a visitor
checks.setup: A published project with two accepted contributors, each with a statement
checks.expected_behavior: Each accepted contributor is shown with their standardized role, their own contribution statement, and the maintainer is identified. Invited-but-unaccepted people are absent.

checks.method_or_action: GET with each row of project_duplicate_cases.json; in the browser the warning appears on leaving the repository or title field in the Add Project form
checks.setup: An existing project whose repository is the one being checked
checks.expected_behavior: exact_repository_duplicate returns advice 'warn_existing_project' with a link to view/join the existing project. similar_title_different_repository returns 'warn_if_useful_but_do_not_auto_merge'. same_title_different_domain returns 'allow_distinct_project_do_not_auto_merge'. No case merges or blocks: creation always remains possible. Repository URLs differing only by scheme, www., .git or a trailing slash normalise to one match.

checks.method_or_action: Read the project twice, save once, then save again with the first (now stale) version value
checks.setup: projects.version is returned by GET /api/my/projects/{id} and must be echoed in the PUT body
checks.expected_behavior: The second save returns 409 with conflict=true and the current record, and does NOT overwrite the first writer's change. The editor re-displays the saved version while keeping the user's typed title and description so they can merge and retry.

checks.method_or_action: Set playable_url, video_url and the repository list independently
checks.setup: None
checks.expected_behavior: Playable web URL, video/demo URL and source/repository URLs are stored and returned in three separate fields. A project may have any subset, including none.

checks.method_or_action: Submit playable_url 'javascript:alert(1)', video_url '<iframe src=//evil.test></iframe>', fallback_image_url 'data:text/html;base64,...' and a fallback_note containing <script>
checks.setup: None
checks.expected_behavior: Only http(s) URLs are stored; all three hostile values are rejected and persisted as empty strings. Markup in text fields is stripped to inert text. The public project page contains no iframe and builds links through the DOM, so no student-supplied markup is ever injected.

checks.method_or_action: Open a published project that has a playable_url
checks.setup: playable_url set to https://team08-r1-frontend.onrender.com/demo/working_demo.html
checks.expected_behavior: An 'Experience this project' section offers a clear 'Play demo' action that opens the demo in a new tab.

checks.method_or_action: Open a project with fallback_image_url and fallback_note set
checks.setup: fallback_image_url set to https://team08-r1-frontend.onrender.com/demo/fallback.svg
checks.expected_behavior: The fallback image and note are shown even when a playable URL also exists, because the playable one may not run on the visitor's device.

checks.method_or_action: Set playable_url and fallback_image_url to unreachable hosts, then open the public page
checks.setup: Any published project
checks.expected_behavior: The project page, the contributor list, the student profile and site navigation all still render. Nothing is iframed, so a dead demo cannot block the page. A fallback image that fails to load is replaced by a text message rather than a broken-image icon, and the fallback note remains readable.

checks.method_or_action: Open each at a 390 CSS pixel viewport width
checks.setup: None
checks.expected_behavior: Project details, contributor roles and fallback evidence remain readable and operable, with no horizontal scrolling on any of the three pages.

checks.method_or_action: Signed in as a student who is neither maintainer nor contributor, PUT against another project's id
checks.role: verified student, unrelated to the project
checks.setup: Any project id, for example the R1 fixture id P01
checks.expected_behavior: 403. Authorization is resolved from the project row and the session, never from a body field, so substituting a project identifier in the request changes nothing. /project-edit.html?id=P01 shows a 'Not your project' explanation rather than an editor.

checks.method_or_action: Run the R1 journeys: directory, search, skill filters, profile, project, employer inquiry; then the R2 profile, privacy and publication flows
checks.setup: The r1-v1 fixtures, loaded automatically on first boot
checks.expected_behavior: The directory still lists 17 published students, filters and inquiry still work, unpublished students remain invisible, and R2 profile editing, per-field privacy, presentation and publication are unchanged. tests/e2e.js covers this and passes 26/26.

checks.method_or_action: Note the URL, transfer maintenance, add and remove repositories, then re-open the same URL
checks.setup: A published project
checks.expected_behavior: The canonical project keeps one stable public identity and URL across maintainer transfer and repository changes.

checks.method_or_action: Resolve the tag and compare with the commit recorded in R3_release_submission.md
checks.setup: None
checks.expected_behavior: The tag R3-submission exists and names the commit recorded as the assessed version.

fixture_setup: The Release 1 fixtures (students.json, skills.json, projects.json) import automatically the first time the backend boots against an empty database, and can be re-imported with `node backend/import.js`. The Release 3 fixtures are used as follows: data/standard_roles.json is the contributor role vocabulary served by GET /api/projects/options and enforced on every invite and role change; project_duplicate_cases.json drives the duplicate-check scenarios above and is asserted verbatim in tests/r3-api.js; working_demo.html and fallback.svg are hosted on our own static site at /demo/working_demo.html and /demo/fallback.svg and used as the playable and fallback URLs of the QA project. The migrations schema.sql, schema_r2.sql and schema_r3.sql run in order on every boot and are idempotent and additive.
test_access: A reviewer signs in with their own GitHub account at /account.html and verifies with an @algomau.ca address, which creates a verified student able to add projects. No account of ours is needed and no password or token is required anywhere. For the shared-project checks (R3.05, R3.09, R3.11, R3.15) use the published QA project named in R3_release_submission.md, which already has two accepted contributors. Two reviewers signing in with two GitHub accounts can exercise the whole invite/accept/decline cycle themselves. Any additional setup is supplied through the approved private course channel.

automated_suites.tests/r3-api.js: 50 checks over the R3 route surface: authorization boundaries, the lost-update conflict, invitation visibility, soft-delete and restore, URL rejection, and all three project_duplicate_cases.json rows. Run with DATABASE_URL and BASE_URL set. Cleans up the synthetic students it creates.
automated_suites.tests/r3-ui.js: 27 browser checks over the Add Project, GitHub import, invite, accept, contribution, publish, Play-demo, broken-demo and 390px journeys.
automated_suites.tests/e2e.js: 26 browser checks over the Release 1 requirements, used as the R3.25 regression gate.
